text: The subject, Danish Shafiq, a low‑risk freelance software developer, received a flurry of inbound IBFT transfers from at least ten distinct counterparties between 4 Aug and 9 Aug 2026, totalling roughly PKR 1,020,000. The inbound amounts range from PKR 16,000 to PKR 86,000 and involve multiple synthetic banks and repeat names (e.g., Waqas Shafiq, Fahad Saeed). Within the same 14‑day window the account executed two unusually large outbound movements: a PKR 195,000 wallet transfer to a QuickPay wallet on 7 Aug and two cash withdrawals of PKR 196,000 and PKR 62,000 from an ATM in Islamabad on 11 Aug. The rapid conversion of inbound funds into cash and a wallet transfer, without any apparent business justification, matches the “border mule” typology (many distinct inbound counterparties, large share of inbound value leaves quickly). The subject’s declared monthly income (PKR 140,000) is far below the volume of transactions, and no adverse media or sanctions hits were found. These patterns indicate possible structuring and money‑laundering activity, warranting a Suspicious Transaction Report.
